instructions:
Classify the overall aerial scene in the image into exactly one of the supplied AID scene classes. Select the class that best describes the scene as a whole, rather than every object visible. Use only the image.

Use the following class descriptions. Keep the supplied class names as the output choices.

Airport: An aviation facility with runways, taxiways, aprons, terminals, or parked aircraft.
BareLand: Exposed soil or rock with little vegetation, often showing clearing, grading, excavation, or other human disturbance.
BaseballField: A baseball or softball playing area recognizable by a diamond-shaped infield and a fan-shaped outfield.
Beach: A sandy or pebbly strip along a shoreline, with adjacent water and exposed shore forming the main scene.
Bridge: A road or railway structure crossing water or another obstacle, with the crossing itself as the principal feature.
Center: A public cultural or event center, such as a theater, generally organized around a prominent purpose-built building.
Church: A church building or church complex, recognizable from its religious architecture and surrounding grounds.
Commercial: A commercial area occupied mainly by shops, offices, or business complexes and their associated access and parking.
DenseResidential: A residential neighborhood with closely packed buildings and relatively little open ground between them.
Desert: An arid landscape dominated by sand, rock, or dry ground, with sparse vegetation and few visible signs of land modification.
Farmland: Land organized for agriculture, with cultivated fields, crop rows, orchards, or recognizable agricultural parcels.
Forest: Land dominated by a broad, continuous or closely grouped cover of trees.
Industrial: An area of factories, production facilities, warehouses, service yards, or industrial equipment.
Meadow: Open land dominated by grass or low herbaceous vegetation, without a clear pattern of crop cultivation.
MediumResidential: A residential neighborhood with noticeable spacing between buildings and a mixture of housing, gardens, trees, and open ground.
Mountain: A landscape dominated by mountainous relief, such as ridges, peaks, and steep slopes, whether vegetated, rocky, or snowy.
Park: A landscaped recreation area with paths, vegetation, and leisure or amusement facilities.
Parking: An area whose principal function is vehicle parking, recognizable from organized parking spaces, aisles, or rows of parked vehicles.
Playground: An outdoor sports field, running track, or playing area without the prominent surrounding spectator stands characteristic of a stadium.
Pond: A contained inland body of standing water, including a natural or constructed pond or a group of ponds.
Port: A harbor, marina, or shipping facility with docks, piers, berths, or vessels beside sheltered water.
RailwayStation: A railway facility centered on station platforms, train sheds, parallel tracks, or associated rail yards.
Resort: A vacation or leisure accommodation complex, often with villas or lodging buildings arranged among landscaped recreation facilities.
River: An elongated natural watercourse, with a connected channel and banks forming the principal scene.
School: An educational campus whose buildings, courtyards, internal paths, and possible sports facilities form a coherent school complex.
SparseResidential: A residential area with a small number of widely separated homes and extensive open land, gardens, or vegetation between them.
Square: A public plaza or formal civic open space, often with organized paving, paths, monuments, or geometric landscaping.
Stadium: A sports venue with substantial spectator stands arranged around a playing field or arena.
StorageTanks: A storage facility dominated by large tanks, often circular or cylindrical and arranged in groups.
Viaduct: An extended elevated road or railway, or a grade-separated road interchange with flyovers and connecting ramps.
image_policy: All controls and transformed variants are 600x600 RGB lossless PNG; control preserves decoded RGB pixels; no resizing.
scoring: Failed requests count as incorrect; same 30-way choice validation as original eval

transform_protocol.selection: 10 per class from test, lowest SHA256(seed+filename); independent of predictions
transform_protocol.image_policy: All controls and transformed variants are 600x600 RGB lossless PNG; control preserves decoded RGB pixels; no resizing.

transformations.shift: 60 pixels left/right with reflected fill; crops 60 original boundary pixels, so this is not pure object-position isolation

transform_protocol.analysis: Paired accuracy changes vs fresh control; McNemar tests; pairwise differences of change via paired randomization; Holm across 30 within-model and 60 between-model tests.
notes: Equal-class balanced subset; accuracy is not directly comparable to the full test split.
Ground truth held fixed; stronger transforms may remove discriminative evidence.
Single stochastic response per model/image/condition; repeat on independent data to confirm.
transform_protocol.control: Fresh clean PNG predictions with the same definitions prompt as every transformation; never use full-test or historical accuracy as the control.
